scope: Before the slides of 2008, 2013 and 2015, it had raised both fuels by 22 percent or more inside the twelve months my test uses as "before" (Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2014; Menteri Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2008, 2013).
inventory: 6 items: the one sentence gate scope --since 3 lists, its paragraph, chart 1's footnote after its sentence was deleted, amendment 8.9 as revised, the 2015 fuel records, and the shared gate's revised mask
method: Each lens refuted its primary items and any others it chose; one skeptic per lens re-checked every non-confirmed finding, in order, and a finding stands only if its skeptic upheld it.

findings.claim: Before the slides of 2008, 2013 and 2015, it had raised both fuels by 22 percent or more inside the twelve months my test uses as "before" (Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2014; Menteri Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2008, 2013).
findings.evidence:
lens P (post text and charts): The only change between rounds is the deletion. Diffing draft/.rounds/3.json against 4.json shows nothing else changed. The paragraph in site/src/content/blog/if-msci-drops-indonesia.mdx matches draft.md:43 byte for byte.

Truth: the src.md:43 bindings resolve to results.json household.fuel.slowed. The rises are 2008-05-23 (+33.3 / +27.9), 2013-06-22 (+44.4 / +22.2) and 2014-11-18 (+30.8 / +36.4). min_pct is 22.2, printed as 22, and every value is at least 22. Each date falls inside the window household.py fuel_list uses (the slide month and the 11 months before it): 2007-11 to 2008-10, 2012-09 to 2013-08 and 2014-10 to 2015-09. That is the 'twelve months' (rules.inflation_window_months) the chart 3 row labels '12 months to the slide'.

Citations: each cited entry's stored document holds its fact.
- Kementerian ESDM 2014 (sources/fuel/esdm_2014-11-18_siaran_pers_60_SJI_2014.html) has the HARGA LAMA/BARU table '6.500 8.500' and '5.500 7.500', in force from 18 Nopember 2014. It also states the 2013 rises: 'harga bensin premium naik menjadi Rp. 6.500/liter (44,4%), sedangkan solar naik menjadi Rp. 5.500/liter (51,1%)'.
- The Menteri ESDM 2008 abstract has 'Bensin Premium : Rp 6.000,00' and 'Minyak Solar (Gas Oil) : Rp 5.500,00', 'Ditetapkan ... 23 Mei 2008'. It names Perpres 55/2005, whose Rp 4.500 / 4.300 is the old price. I checked that with pdftotext on perpres_55_2005.pdf, lines 124 and 127.
- Menteri ESDM 2013 (Permen 18/2013) has Rp 6.500 / 5.500 from 22 Juni 2013.

The in-text order (Kementerian before Menteri, 2008 before 2013) matches the reference list. Read as 'a rise of at least 22 percent happened inside the window', the sentence is true for all three slides. Whether it is still fair after the deletion is item 2.

findings.claim: The fuel paragraph of the prices section as it now reads in full, after round 3 deleted ', though in the year before the 2015 slide it also cut them two times' (uncited): is it still accurate, cited and balanced against chart 3 directly below it?
findings.evidence:
lens P (post text and charts): I read the whole paragraph (draft.md:43; identical in the MDX) with chart 3 below it.

What still holds:
- October 2005: +87.5 / +104.8. The Perpres 55/2005 PDF has Rp 4.500 / 4.300 from 1 Oktober 2005. The old prices 2.400 / 2.100 ('sekitar 87%', 'sekitar 105%') are in the Kementerian 2014 release, which is cited in the next sentence.
- The cuts after 2008 and 2015 match results.json, and Ditjen Migas 2016 holds '5.650 5.150' and 'Premium RON 88 Penugasan Luar Jawa-Madura-Bali 6.950 6.450'.
- The Bank Indonesia sentence matches the stored page (sources/provenance/ojk-bps/bi_inflasi_definisi.txt): 'kenaikan harga BBM di tahun 2005 dan 2008, sehingga menyebabkan adanya lonjakan inflasi'.
- The paragraph uses no causal word of the author's own.

The defect: round 3 deleted the only words in the prose saying the 2015 'before' window did not only go up. The paragraph now runs 'Before the slides of 2008, 2013 and 2015, it had raised both fuels by 22 percent or more ... It cut them in the year after the 2008 and 2015 slides', which presents 2015 as a one-way rise before the slide and cuts after it.

Computed check (lens-P/net_2015.py, which reads the stored notices and asserts each passage):
- migas_2015-03-28 has '2 Bensin Premium RON 88 6.800 7.300', and esdm_2015-10-10 has 'Sementara harga Premium tetap Rp 7.300'. So in the slide month the government-set Premium price was Rp 7,300.
- Before the 18 Nov 2014 rise it was Rp 6,500. Net change over the window: +12.3%.
- The two January 2015 cuts and later changes undid 60% of the November Premium rise. Solar's net change was +25.5%.

A reader who takes 'raised both fuels by 22 percent or more inside the twelve months' as how far prices climbed over the window is wrong about Premium in 2015 by about half. That includes a worried family member and an Indonesian economist checking the January 2015 reversal.

Chart 3 prints '3 rises, 2 cuts' under Sep 2015. That shows cuts happened, but not that they undid most of the Premium rise, and three rises against two cuts suggests prices ended up higher. The sentence is still true as a statement about one change, so the severity is LOW. | skeptic upheld: I upheld this at LOW severity. Each word of the sentence is true, but the paragraph is unbalanced against chart 3, and a reader who takes the 22 percent as the net change over the window gets 2015 Premium wrong. Inventory item 2 asks about exactly this balance, so I do not count it as a style preference.

What I checked myself:
(1) draft.md line 43 and the site MDX (joechrisnaldy-portfolio/site/src/content/blog/if-msci-drops-indonesia.mdx) have the same paragraph; a diff prints nothing. The cut clause appears in no other paragraph: a grep finds 2015 only on lines 41, 43 and 87.
(2) round3-verdicts.json line 59 shows the old clause ', though in the year before the 2015 slide it also cut them two times'. Lines 61 and 63 record that round 3 deleted it only because nothing cited it, and relied on chart 3 to show the cuts.
(3) The stored notices give this government-set price chain over the 2014-10 to 2015-09 window (household.py's before window, per the round 3 record):
- esdm_2014-11-18 table: '6.500 8.500' (Premium) and '5.500 7.500' (Solar).
- esdm_2015-01-01: Premium 'menjadi Rp 7.600', Solar 'Rp 7.250'.
- esdm_2015-01-19: Premium 'Rp 7600/liter menjadi Rp 6.600'; Solar Rp 6,400 per the manifest.
- migas_2015-03-01: Premium outside Java-Madura-Bali 6,600 to 6,800.
- migas_2015-03-28: '1 Minyak Solar 6.400 6.900 2 Bensin Premium RON 88 6.800 7.300'.
- esdm_2015-10-10: 'Sementara harga Premium tetap Rp 7.300'.
(4) My script (skeptic-P/net_check.py) gives Premium a net +12.3% (6,500 to 7,300) and Solar +25.5% (5,500 to 6,900). The January cuts and the later changes undid 60% of the November 2014 Premium rise. All match the finding.
(5) The sentence's 22 comes from results.json household.fuel.slowed (episodes 27.9, 22.2, 30.8; min_pct 22.2). Read as a single rise, the sentence holds for 2015 (30.8/36.4). Read as the net change over the window, it fails for Premium.
(6) Chart 3 (charts/mf-3-prices.png) prints '3 rises, 2 cuts' under Sep 2015. That shows the cuts happened but not their size.

One caveat on the finding's evidence. The +12.3% is for the government-set price, which from March 2015 is the price outside Java-Madura-Bali; draft line 87 discloses this. The Java price at the slide is unverified. Pertamina's January 2016 table gives Java's old price as 7,400, which would make about +13.8% if it was unchanged since September 2015. That is still well under 22, so the conclusion stands.

Checking the proposed fix:
- Kementerian 2014 is the only cited source for the 2013 figures (44,4%, Solar to Rp 5.500). It does not mention 2008, which Menteri 2008 covers.
- It also prints '(51,1%)' for the 2013 Solar rise, against 22.2% computed from 4,500 to 5,500. This was already in the draft before the fix, and 51.1 is still 22 or more.
- Kementerian 2014 must stay: it is the only source in the reference list that gives the 2005 old prices (2.400 and 2.100). Presiden 2005 is Perpres 55/2005, which has the new prices only.
- The 2015-09 slide key is still used in the next sentence, and min_pct still prints 22.
findings.fix: Narrowed 'Before the slides of 2008, 2013 and 2015' to 'Before the slides of 2008 and 2013' (the 2015 before-window rise was largely undone by the January 2015 cuts); the printed 22 is household.fuel.slowed.min_pct, the 2013 Solar rise, so it still holds for the two slides named; all three citations still support the sentence; chart 3 keeps the 2015 counts.

If you want it trimmed...', and at 00:59:19Z offered again to trim 'from about 2,780 words toward 2,300'. The owner asked at 00:57:44Z to change Java to Jakarta, which shows the draft was read. findings.claim: The several-year citation mask (_CITE_YEARS) now applies only inside a full '(...)' of the post body; README and published templates keep the single-year mask. Does any wrong citation or unbound number now pass that the gate before round 2 caught? Do the gate's tests pass?
findings.evidence:
lens R (records and gate): The tests pass. In place, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s gate/tests -t .` gives 'Ran 246 tests ... OK'. HEAD (a git archive in lens-R/old) gives 243 OK. HEAD's code with the new test files fails 3 (lens-R/redcheck2). Round 2's code (scratchpad/round3/skeptic-L/new) fails the new test_several_years_are_masked_only_in_a_post_citation (lens-R/r2code), so that test did fail first. The diff matches the record: _CITE_YEARS is applied only inside _PAREN spans when readme=False (numbers.py:39-41, :82-83), and templates still use readme=True (numbers.py:142). README and published templates show no regression: lens-R/probe_r.py (old against new) flags '(Dell, 2007, 2009)', '(Dell et al., 2007, 1850)', '(Dell, 2007, 2010)' and '(Indonesia, 2005, 2008, 2020)' in both versions. In the body, '; Jakarta, 1850, 1900)' and '; Jakarta, 2005, 2008;' are flagged in both. Wrong years are caught by cite: '(Dell, 2007, 2010)', '(Dell, 2007, 1850)', '(Jakarta, 2005, 2008)', '(Kementerian ..., 2008, 2013)' and '(Dell, 2007, 2009a)'. Hidden figures stay caught: '(Dell, 2007, 2009, 12.5)', '(Dell, 2007, 2009, p. 12.5)', '(by 1.1 points; Dell, 2007, 2009)'. But in the post body, wrong citations that HEAD caught now pass. HEAD reported their years as unbound numbers; the new gate masks them, and cite.check matches an entry when its first surname occurs anywhere in the names (cite.py:66). Examples, with reference entries Dell (2007) and Dell (2009) as single-author works and Bank Indonesia (2024, 2026a): '(Smith & Dell, 2007, 2009)', '(Jones and Dell, 2007, 2009)', '(Dell et al., 2007, 2009)', '(rose by Dell, 2007, 2009)' and '(Bank Indonesia Research Unit, 2024, 2026a)'. A second class: a placeholder in a citation's name part that renders a digit. '(Dell {{x.v:int}}, 2007, 2010)' passes even though no Dell 2010 entry exists. numbers.check masks the years in the .src.md template, while cite.check reads the rendered 'Dell 3', whose digit stops _SEGMENT from matching (__main__.py runs numbers on source and cite on rendered). Both classes already pass at HEAD for one-year citations (lens-R/probe_single.py: '(Smith & Dell, 2007)', '(Dell et al., 2009)' and '(Dell {{x.v:int}}, 2010)' pass in old and new). So the change raises several-year citations to the one-year standard and no further, and it widens the same kind of gap round 3 refuted in round 2's version. Post 27 is unaffected: its only several-year citations are '(Menteri Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2008, 2013)' and '(Indonesia Stock Exchange, 2007, 2009, 2021)', whose names match their entries exactly. New cite.check on the draft returns 0 findings, where the old one reported 5 'never cited'. Of the gated posts, only Post 27 has such citations. | skeptic upheld: I reran everything in skeptic-R using my own copies: old = `git archive HEAD gate` (HEAD 660cb27, the last commit to touch gate/, so the pre-round-2 gate), new = the working tree (`diff -rq` against the repo shows no differences).

Tests. New: 'Ran 246 tests ... OK'. Old: 243 OK. Old code with the new test files: 3 failures (the two cite tests and test_a_citation_parenthetical_cannot_hide_a_figure). Round 2's code (round3/skeptic-L/new) with the new tests: 1 failure, test_several_years_are_masked_only_in_a_post_citation, so that test did fail first.

The diff matches the record. numbers.py:39-41 defines _PAREN and _CITE_YEARS, :82-83 applies them only when readme is false, and :142 still renders templates with readme=True.

What stays caught (skeptic-R/probe.py, p_old.json against p_new.json):
- Templates still flag '(Dell, 2007, 2009)', '(Dell et al., 2007, 1850)', '(Dell, 2007, 2010)' and '(Indonesia, 2005, 2008, 2020)' in both versions.
- The body still flags '; Jakarta, 1850, 1900)' and '; Jakarta, 2005, 2008;' in both.
- The new cite check catches wrong years: '(Dell, 2007, 2010)', '(Dell, 2007, 1850)', '(Dell, 2007, 2009a)', '(Jakarta, 2005, 2008)' and '(Kementerian Energi, 2008, 2014)'.
- Hidden figures stay unbound: '(Dell, 2007, 2009, 12.5)', '(Dell, 2007, 2009, p. 12.5)', and the '1.1' in '(by 1.1 points; Dell, 2007, 2009)'.

Regressions confirmed. My test entries were single-author Dell (2007) and Dell (2009), plus Bank Indonesia (2024, 2026a). Old reports the years of each of these as unbound numbers; new returns 0 findings from both the numbers check and the cite check:
- '(Smith & Dell, 2007, 2009)'
- '(Jones and Dell, 2007, 2009)'
- '(Dell et al., 2007, 2009)'
- '(rose by Dell, 2007, 2009)'
- '(Bank Indonesia Research Unit, 2024, 2026a)'

The cause is cite.py:66. It accepts any entry whose surname, the author text before the first comma, appears as a whole word anywhere in the names.

The placeholder class is also real. The gate runs numbers.check on the source and cite.check on the rendered text (gate/__main__.py:115, :128). In '(Dell {{x.v:int}}, 2007, 2010)' the numbers check masks the years in the source, but the rendered 'Dell 3' has a digit, so cite's _SEGMENT never parses the segment. Old flags 2007 and 2010; new passes, although no 2010 entry exists. Two more forms behave the same way: '(Dell, {{x.v:int}}, 2007, 2010)' and a more natural one, '(up {{x.v:int}} points, Dell, 2007, 2010)'. In these cases the comment's claim that the cite check 'verifies each year against its entry' is plainly false, because the cite check never sees those years.

All of these holes already exist for one-year citations. Old passes '(Smith & Dell, 2007)', '(Dell et al., 2009)' and '(Dell {{x.v:int}}, 2010)'. So the change widens existing gaps. That is the same standard round 3 used to refute round 2's version (r3:item:32: 'the change widens existing gaps').

Post 27 is unaffected:
- Its only several-year citations are 'Menteri Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2008, 2013' and 'Indonesia Stock Exchange, 2007, 2009, 2021', and the names match their entries exactly.
- On the draft, the new cite check gives 0 findings and the old one gives 5 'never cited'.
- The old numbers check flags 5 unbound years in the source (lines 43 and 92); the new one flags none.
- reversal-of-fortune and safe-haven-retest have no several-year citations.

The finding missed one place with the same overclaim: the comment at gate/tests/test_numbers_pairs.py:159 ('the cite check verifies each year only inside a full (...) of the post').

The proposed replacement wording is still false for the placeholder class, since the cite check never matches those years. It also adds a comparative claim ('the same test a one-year citation gets').
findings.fix: Narrowed the comments that overstated the cite check: numbers.py now says only where the several-year mask applies, and the test comment likewise. Record note: round 3's fix text 'where cite.check verifies each year' overstates the check; it matches each year to an entry whose surname appears in the citation, the same test a one-year citation gets. 246 gate tests pass.
